doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Moving to online teaching, including a Tokyo student
summary: She had not taught on Zoom before; a Tokyo lesson reminds her of a cancelled Japan pre-Olympics gig, and she plans to use online platforms like TrueFire.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah. With your online lessons, was this something you were doing before now?

No. I was teaching — I have a student here. I wasn’t teaching. I did the occasional FaceTime lesson, from the road often. Never did the Zoom format before, never. Now yesterday I taught a student, and this was very interesting, I taught a student in Tokyo early in the morning because of the time difference. And he said, “Last night you would have been performing 400 meters up the street from here.” And that hit home, I was like, “That’s right I was going to be in Japan.” It was a big pre-Olympics thing with an all-girl Japanese orchestra and I was going to be the band leader. And it was going to be really exciting because they put together this really cool thing with all these Japanese women. It was going to be really fun. And the gig was cancelled of course, so the tour cancelled, even though I think Japan is recovering quite well actually, right now. And that was like, “Oh that’s right, wow, yeah. Well thank you for having a lesson.” You know. So you get little odd things like that, yeah, this is a different reality. We don’t know what’s coming out of this reality for musicians, you know what I mean? So online teaching and online
forums like TrueFire and other mediums like that, that’s where I’m going to get stuck into because that’s what I need to be doing right now.
